Practice-relevant•Peer-reviewed biomarker analysis of a phase 3 randomized trial•August 7, 2026

Plasma p-tau217 did not identify amyloid clearance after donanemab

Among donanemab-treated TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 participants, plasma p-tau217 had an AUC of 0.61 at week 52 for detecting PET amyloid below 24.1 Centiloids, so the blood marker could not substitute for PET when determining individual treatment-related amyloid clearance.

Key quantitative results: In 830 donanemab-treated participants, p-tau217 AUC for amyloid clearance was 0.61 at week 52.

BiomarkersBloodp-tau217AmyloidDisease monitoring

Added October 14, 2026 · DOI:10.1002/alz.71740; NCT04437511

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

This is an important boundary condition for blood biomarkers. Plasma p-tau217 decreased with treatment and tracked amyloid change weakly at the group level, but it could not tell whether an individual had reached the PET clearance threshold. Treatment monitoring requires a different validation question from baseline diagnosis.

Study design

Longitudinal secondary analysis of the phase 3 TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 trial. Amyloid PET and plasma biomarkers were measured at baseline and during donanemab treatment. Performance was assessed for treatment-related amyloid clearance defined as PET amyloid below 24.1 Centiloids.

Key quantitative results

  • In 830 donanemab-treated participants, p-tau217 AUC for amyloid clearance was 0.61 at week 52.
  • Amyloid clearance occurred in 66.1% at week 52 and 76.4% at week 76.
  • Change in p-tau217 and change in PET amyloid were weakly correlated at week 52 (r=0.34; p<0.0001).
  • Adding age, APOE ε4, p-tau181, GFAP, and NfL did not provide meaningful individual-level discrimination; the multivariable AUC was 0.71 at week 76.

What changed

The analysis directly tested and rejected the assumption that diagnostic p-tau217 performance automatically extends to individual post-treatment amyloid-clearance monitoring.

Strength of evidence

Moderate-to-strong negative clinical-validity evidence from a large phase 3 trial dataset with longitudinal PET and two p-tau217 assay approaches; the analysis was secondary and specific to donanemab-treated early symptomatic AD.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

A lower plasma p-tau217 result should not be interpreted as proof that an individual has reached the PET amyloid-clearance threshold after donanemab.

Field medical relevance

Highly useful for field questions about treatment-response biomarkers, PET replacement, stopping decisions, and why cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy does not establish longitudinal monitoring utility.

Quanterix or platform relevance

The negative individual-level result is platform-relevant: falling p-tau217 can show a group treatment effect without reliably establishing that a given patient crossed the PET amyloid-clearance threshold.

Access or reimbursement relevance

A validated blood stopping rule could reduce PET burden, but these data do not support that substitution and therefore do not establish an access or cost benefit.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Can serial p-tau217 replace amyloid PET after donanemab?
No. Individual-level discrimination for PET-defined clearance was suboptimal.
Does p-tau217 still fall with treatment?
Yes, at the group level, but the decline did not reliably identify which individual crossed the PET threshold.
Would adding other blood markers solve the problem?
Not in this analysis; the multivariable model did not provide meaningful discrimination.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Secondary analysis
  • Donanemab-specific population and treatment protocol
  • PET threshold-specific endpoint
  • Monitoring result should not be generalized to baseline diagnostic use
  • No alternative blood stopping rule was validated
